name: Does an ADU bathroom need a shower to be considered legal?

mainEntity.name: Can an ADU have only a toilet and sink, or does it need a shower or tub too?
mainEntity.text: Can an ADU have only a toilet and sink, or does it need a shower or tub too?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an ADU, a toilet and sink alone are usually not enough for a fully functional independent living unit. Most ADUs are designed as complete dwelling spaces, so the bathroom normally includes a shower or tub in addition to the toilet and lavatory. The exact requirements can vary by project type, but from a planning standpoint the bathroom should be treated as a complete bathing and sanitation room rather than a powder room. This matters because the room size, ventilation, waterproofing, and plumbing layout all change once a shower is included. Homeowners sometimes try to start with a simple half-bath concept and later discover it does not support the intended use of the ADU. The safest approach is to decide early whether the unit will be a true independent living space, then size the bathroom accordingly. If space is tight, a compact shower pan, pocket door, and stacked fixture layout can help keep the room functional without wasting square footage.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU bathroom typically needs full sanitation fixtures that support independent living, which usually means a toilet, sink, and bathing facility such as a shower or tub. A half-bath may work for other parts of a house, but it usually does not meet the expectations for a self-contained ADU. Confirm the fixture set during design, not after construction starts.
